```{r setup}
project_root <- rprojroot::find_rstudio_root_file()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)
setwd(project_root)

# To add a new package: renv::install("packageName") or renv::install("bioc::packageName"), then renv::snapshot(). Snapshots are always run in the console

pacman::p_load(Seurat, Signac, GenomicRanges, JASPAR2024, TFBSTools, BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10, tidyverse, Matrix, patchwork, BiocParallel)

# chromVAR in parallel; Seurat runs sequentially, as each worker would get a 6 GB copy of the data
register(SnowParam(workers = 4))
set.seed(1234)

# Mouse hindlimb muscle at E14.5, E18.5, P5 and adult, 10x Multiome (Dos Santos et al. 2023, GSE211543), one library per stage.
# Processed following the authors' script (github.com/matthieudossantos/Multiome-snRNAseq-and-snATACseq-Muscle-development-atlas-script).
# Only difference: their fragment files are not deposited, so ATAC counts are the deposited per-library peak counts summed over
# the merged peaks, instead of fragments counted in them. Only merged peaks called in all four libraries are kept, as the others
# are zero by construction in the libraries that did not call them, which separates the libraries
raw_dir  <- "revision/A1_sc_cross_species/mammalian_sc_data/Mouse_Muscle_Development_DosSantos2023"
data_dir <- "in_vivo_mouse_muscle_development/data"
res_dir  <- "in_vivo_mouse_muscle_development/results"

samples <- c("E14.5" = "GSM6475260_E14", "E18.5" = "GSM6475261_E18", "P5" = "GSM6475262_P5", "Adult" = "GSM6475263_Adult")
```


# Preparing Data

```{r counts}
# One library: RNA counts per gene, ATAC counts per peak called in that library, and the peak positions
read_sample <- function(id, stage) {
  counts   <- readMM(file.path(raw_dir, paste0(id, "_matrix.mtx.gz")))
  features <- read.delim(file.path(raw_dir, paste0(id, "_features.tsv.gz")), header = FALSE) # V2 gene or peak, V3 type, V4-V6 position
  barcodes <- read.delim(file.path(raw_dir, paste0(id, "_barcodes.tsv.gz")), header = FALSE)
  colnames(counts) <- paste(stage, barcodes$V1, sep = "_")

  genes <- features$V3 == "Gene Expression"
  rna <- counts[genes, ]
  rownames(rna) <- make.unique(features$V2[genes])

  peaks <- features$V3 == "Peaks"
  ranges <- GRanges(seqnames = features$V4[peaks],
                    ranges = IRanges(start = features$V5[peaks] + 1, end = features$V6[peaks])) # 0-based starts in the file

  list(rna = as(rna, "CsparseMatrix"), atac = counts[peaks, ], ranges = ranges)
}

data <- Map(read_sample, id = samples, stage = names(samples))

# Merged peaks of the four libraries, 20 bp to 10 kb, standard chromosomes
merged <- GenomicRanges::reduce(c(data$E14.5$ranges, data$E18.5$ranges, data$P5$ranges, data$Adult$ranges)) # GenomicRanges, not purrr
merged <- merged[width(merged) > 20 & width(merged) < 10000]
merged <- GenomeInfoDb::keepStandardChromosomes(merged, species = "Mus_musculus", pruning.mode = "coarse")

# Only merged peaks called in all four libraries
called_in_all <- overlapsAny(merged, data$E14.5$ranges) & overlapsAny(merged, data$E18.5$ranges) &
  overlapsAny(merged, data$P5$ranges) & overlapsAny(merged, data$Adult$ranges)
merged <- merged[called_in_all]

# One Seurat object per library. ATAC: the counts of the library's peaks summed over the merged peak each one overlaps
objects <- imap(data, function(x, stage) {
  hits <- findOverlaps(query = x$ranges, subject = merged)
  peak_to_merged <- sparseMatrix(i = subjectHits(hits), j = queryHits(hits), x = 1,
                                 dims = c(length(merged), length(x$ranges))) # merged peaks x library peaks, 1 = overlap
  atac <- peak_to_merged %*% x$atac
  rownames(atac) <- GRangesToString(merged)

  obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = x$rna, project = stage)
  obj[["ATAC"]] <- CreateChromatinAssay(counts = atac)
  obj
})

seu <- merge(objects[[1]], y = objects[-1])
seu$stage <- factor(seu$orig.ident, levels = names(samples))
seu[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(seu, pattern = "^mt-", assay = "RNA")
```


# QC

```{r qc}
# Thresholds of the authors' script. TSS enrichment and nucleosome signal would need the fragment files
seu <- subset(seu, subset = nCount_ATAC < 7e4 & nCount_ATAC > 400 & nCount_RNA < 25000 & nCount_RNA > 400 & percent.mt < 20)
```


# Integration

```{r integration}
# RNA: SCTransform per library with the mitochondrial reads regressed, RPCA anchors
DefaultAssay(seu) <- "RNA"
seu <- JoinLayers(seu)

seu_list <- SplitObject(seu, split.by = "stage")
seu_list <- lapply(seu_list, function(x) {
  x <- NormalizeData(x)
  x <- FindVariableFeatures(x, nfeatures = 2000)
  SCTransform(x, method = "glmGamPoi", vars.to.regress = "percent.mt")
})

anchor_features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = seu_list, nfeatures = 3000)
seu_list <- PrepSCTIntegration(object.list = seu_list, anchor.features = anchor_features)
seu_list <- lapply(seu_list, RunPCA, features = anchor_features)

anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(object.list = seu_list, normalization.method = "SCT", anchor.features = anchor_features,
                                  dims = 1:30, reduction = "rpca", k.anchor = 20)
seu <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors, normalization.method = "SCT", new.assay.name = "integratedRNA", dims = 1:30)

# ATAC: LSI, then integrated with the same anchors
DefaultAssay(seu) <- "ATAC"
seu <- RunTFIDF(seu)
seu <- FindTopFeatures(seu, min.cutoff = "q25")
seu <- RunSVD(seu)

# IntegrateEmbeddings returns a whole new object, only its integratedLSI is kept
seu[["integratedLSI"]] <- IntegrateEmbeddings(anchorset = anchors, reductions = seu[["lsi"]],
                                              new.reduction.name = "integratedLSI")[["integratedLSI"]]

# Weighted neighbours of lsi and integratedLSI, UMAP and clusters (algorithm 3 = SLM), as in the authors' script
seu <- FindMultiModalNeighbors(seu, reduction.list = list("lsi", "integratedLSI"), dims.list = list(1:30, 2:30))
seu <- RunUMAP(seu, nn.name = "weighted.nn", reduction.name = "wnn.umap")
seu <- FindClusters(seu, graph.name = "wsnn", algorithm = 3)

DimPlot(seu, reduction = "wnn.umap", label = TRUE) + DimPlot(seu, reduction = "wnn.umap", group.by = "stage")

ggsave(file.path(res_dir, "umap_all_nuclei.png"), width = 13, height = 5.5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```


# Cell types

```{r normalise}
# Log-normalised RNA of all libraries together, for the marker plot and the saved RNA
DefaultAssay(seu) <- "RNA"
seu <- JoinLayers(seu) # IntegrateData splits the RNA layers by stage again
seu <- NormalizeData(seu)
```

```{r cell-types}
# Clusters named from the marker plot below, with the cell types of the paper
cell_types <- c("1" = "Myonuclei", "2" = "Myonuclei", "3" = "Myonuclei", "4" = "Myonuclei", "8" = "Myonuclei", "11" = "Myonuclei",
                "13" = "Myonuclei", "12" = "Myoblasts", "14" = "Myoblasts", "10" = "MuSCs",
                "0" = "Mesenchymal", "6" = "Mesenchymal", "16" = "Mesenchymal",
                "5" = "Tenocytes", "7" = "Tenocytes", "17" = "Tenocytes", "21" = "Tenocytes",
                "9" = "Endothelial", "15" = "Macrophages", "18" = "Smooth muscle", "20" = "Smooth muscle", # 18: pericytes (Rgs5, Pdgfrb)
                "19" = "Adipocytes")

seu$cell_type <- unname(cell_types[as.character(seu$seurat_clusters)])
seu$stage <- factor(seu$stage, levels = names(samples)) # integration turns it back into text
```

```{r markers}
# Marker genes per cluster, behind the names above: the markers of the paper (Fig. 1c), stage myosins and pericytes (Rgs5, Pdgfrb)
cluster_labels <- paste0(seu$cell_type, " (", seu$seurat_clusters, ")") # e.g. "Myonuclei (1)"
label_order <- paste0(cell_types, " (", names(cell_types), ")") # rows in the order of the table, from the top
seu$label <- factor(cluster_labels, levels = rev(label_order))

marker_genes <- c("Ttn", "Myh3", "Myh8", "Myh4", "Col22a1", "Mymk", "Myog", "Pax7", "Mki67", "Pdgfra", "Tnxb", "Col11a1", "Scx",
                  "Flt1", "Mrc1", "Myh11", "Rgs5", "Pdgfrb", "Pparg")

marker_plot <- DotPlot(seu, features = marker_genes, group.by = "label") +
  RotatedAxis() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Markers per WNN cluster (paper Fig. 1c markers + stage myosins)")

marker_plot

ggsave(filename = file.path(res_dir, "cell_type_markers.png"), plot = marker_plot, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

seu$label <- NULL # only for this plot, the saved objects keep their columns
```

```{r umap-rna}
# RNA UMAP of the integrated RNA, as their Fig. 1b, d
DefaultAssay(seu) <- "integratedRNA"
seu <- seu %>%
  ScaleData() %>%
  RunPCA(npcs = 30) %>%
  RunUMAP(dims = 1:30, reduction.name = "umap.RNA")

DimPlot(seu, reduction = "umap.RNA", group.by = "cell_type", label = TRUE) + NoLegend() +
  DimPlot(seu, reduction = "umap.RNA", group.by = "stage")

ggsave(file.path(res_dir, "umap_cell_types.png"), width = 13, height = 5.5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```


# Motif activity

```{r chromvar}
# chromVAR on all nuclei, as in the paper (Signac AddMotifs and RunChromVAR), with JASPAR 2024 vertebrate CORE (879 motifs,
# EPAS1 included) instead of JASPAR2020 human
jaspar <- RSQLite::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), db(JASPAR2024()))
pfm <- getMatrixSet(jaspar, opts = list(collection = "CORE", tax_group = "vertebrates", all_versions = FALSE))

DefaultAssay(seu) <- "ATAC"
seu <- AddMotifs(seu, genome = BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10, pfm = pfm)

# Signac 1.17 dropped RunChromVAR, so chromVAR is called directly, as RunChromVAR did (a missing GC bias set to 0)
counts <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "ATAC", layer = "counts")
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts), rowRanges = StringToGRanges(rownames(counts)))
se <- chromVAR::addGCBias(se, genome = BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10)
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)$bias[is.na(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)$bias)] <- 0

motif_matches <- GetMotifData(seu, assay = "ATAC") # peaks x motifs
background <- chromVAR::getBackgroundPeaks(se) # GC- and accessibility-matched peaks, drawn after the last seed set above (RunUMAP, 42)
dev <- chromVAR::computeDeviations(se, annotations = motif_matches, background_peaks = background)

seu[["chromvar"]] <- CreateAssayObject(data = chromVAR::deviationScores(dev)) # z-scores
```


# Myogenic nuclei

```{r myogenic}
# Fig. 6B UMAP: MuSCs, myoblasts and myonuclei, with the neighbours of lsi and integratedLSI 
myogenic <- subset(seu, subset = cell_type %in% c("MuSCs", "Myoblasts", "Myonuclei"))
myogenic <- FindMultiModalNeighbors(myogenic, reduction.list = list("lsi", "integratedLSI"), dims.list = list(1:30, 2:30), k.nn = 50)
myogenic <- RunUMAP(myogenic, nn.name = "weighted.nn", reduction.name = "myogenic.umap", min.dist = 0.3, seed.use = 42)
myogenic[["myogenic.umap"]]@cell.embeddings[, 1] <- -myogenic[["myogenic.umap"]]@cell.embeddings[, 1]

DefaultAssay(myogenic) <- "RNA"

DimPlot(myogenic, reduction = "myogenic.umap", group.by = "stage") + DimPlot(myogenic, reduction = "myogenic.umap", group.by = "cell_type") +
  FeaturePlot(myogenic, reduction = "myogenic.umap", features = c("Pax7", "Mymk", "Myh3", "Myh4"), ncol = 2)

ggsave(file.path(res_dir, "umap_myogenic.png"), width = 18, height = 5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```


# Save

```{r save}
# Fig. 6B: log-normalised RNA, the myogenic UMAP, cell_type and stage of the myogenic nuclei
myogenic_rna <- DietSeurat(myogenic, assays = "RNA", layers = "data", dimreducs = "myogenic.umap")
saveRDS(myogenic_rna, file.path(data_dir, "myogenic_rna.rds"))

# Fig. 6B: motif activity (chromVAR z) of the same nuclei, rows named TF.ID (e.g. EPAS1.MA2325.1)
motif_z <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "chromvar", layer = "data")
motif_z <- motif_z[, colnames(myogenic)]
tf_names <- toupper(ConvertMotifID(seu, id = rownames(motif_z), assay = "ATAC"))
rownames(motif_z) <- paste(tf_names, rownames(motif_z), sep = ".")
saveRDS(motif_z, file.path(data_dir, "myogenic_motifs.rds"))
```
